articles.title: FACT CHECK: Plane with drugs not same aircraft used to fly Duterte to The Hague
articles.summary: The tail number of the aircraft used to transport former president Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague does not match that of the jet carrying suspected illegal drugs from Laos, contrary to claims in social…

blocks.text: Claim: The post claimed that the plane found to be carrying illegal drugs from Laos is the same one used in bringing former president Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague.

Why we fact-checked this: Amid recent reports of an aircraft from Laos allegedly carrying illegal drugs bound for the Philippines, a Facebook post by Tinood Politiko, which has garnered nearly 1,000 shares, claimed that the aircraft was the same one used to transport former president Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague, the Netherlands.
The post also used AI-generated photo showing an aircraft and Duterte with the overlay text: “SAME AIRPLANE LEARJET 55B N73GP” and “KATAPATAN BA ITO O MALALIM NA KONEKSYON?”
(Same airplane Learjet 55B N73GP. Is this right or there is a deeper connection?)

The facts: Upon verification, the jet plane flagged in Laos has a tail number showing “N73GP,”a 1986 model of Gates Learjet 55B, which is different from the plane that carried Duterte to The Hague, Netherlands on March 11, 2025.
Reports show that the plane used to to fly Duterte was Gulfstream G550 with tail number “RP-C5219” contrary to the fake post.
The jet plane with alleged illegal drugs was reported by a Malaysian media site, containing 521 kilograms of suspected shabu worth P3.1 million, and is allegedly bound for the Philippines.
One of the plane’s passengers is a Filipino citizen, who reportedly booked the aircraft supposedly to move vape products.
Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) spokesperson Joseph Frederick Calulut shared on October 11 that full details have not been received from the Malaysian authorities.

Ongoing trial: Last October 13, Duterte attended a status conference at the International Criminal Court, prior to his full trial on November 30. The prosecution has presented further evidence against the former president and emphasized their relevance to the drug war campaign.
Duterte will be tried in connection with his crimes against humanity case resulting from his bloody war on drugs. — Axel Cainglet/Rappler.com
Axel John Cainglet is a political science student at the University of the Philippines Manila. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is also the editor-in-chief of The Manila Collegian.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

Despite Lara's office denying any wrongdoing and claiming he divested from JLL Pulsar before taking office, the investigation continues as his family's ownership stake in the company remains significant.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman launched a preliminary investigation into Cagayan 3rd District Representative Jojo Lara for possible plunder.
The probe comes a year after Rappler first reported about Lara’s ties to JLL Pulsar, which has bagged P3.7 billion in contracts from the DPWH since 2020, coinciding with Lara’s congressional career.
“There was supposed to be a divestment, which we think did not really happen,” Ombudsman Boying Remulla told the media on Friday, October 16.
Remulla said the preliminary investigation covers Lara’s connection with JLL Pulsar and JDL5 Construction Corporation, another company believed to be owned by the congressman.
“The money paid to these construction companies still went to his private bank account, with the amount of P1.9 billion,” he added.

Rappler’s original investigation showed that out of the P3.7 billion in public works contracts of JLL Pulsar, P2.1 billion in projects were in Lara’s home province. Around P1.37 billion in contracts were secured since 2023, coinciding with the time he became vice chairperson of the House appropriations committee, which reviews the executive’s proposed national budget annually.

Lara’s office previously denied any wrongdoing, telling Rappler that the congressman removed his shares from JLL Pulsar before he entered public office in 2019. Lara is now in his third and final House term.

“His position as vice chairman of appropriations has nothing to do with this,” Lara’s chief of staff Vic Casauay said in October 2025. “Their contracts have dropped dramatically (since he became a congressman).”
Based on the General Information Sheet submitted by JLL Pulsar to the SEC, Lara’s children own 96.28% of the company as of March 2025.
Joseph Jeremy Lara and Joseph Joshua Lara own 26.2% each; Joseph Kyle Lara owns 23.8%; and Joseph Lara II owns 20.08%. The congressman’s daughter-in-law, Jessa Lara, has a 3.72% stake. – Rappler.com

articles.title: All Pax SIlica issues to be 'properly addressed', says envoy
articles.summary: Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manual “Babe” Romualdez said that all of the issues concerning the controversial Pax Silica initiative will be addressed.
articles.byline: JP SORIANO, JEAN MANGALUZ, GMA News

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 3:24pm

“Obviously, if it's not good for the country, I don't think President Marcos will agree to it. But so far, the way it looks, it's going to be good for the country,” Philippine Ambassador to the Washington Babe Romualdez said.
Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manual “Babe” Romualdez said that all of the issues concerning the controversial Pax Silica initiative will be addressed.

The Pax Silica initiative has been criticized by various groups, with many citing its negative impact on the environment and the possible displacement of local indigenous people. Others criticized the project’s lack of transparency.
“All the issues that are being raised would be properly addressed,” Romualdez said.
“Obviously, if it's not good for the country, I don't think President Marcos will agree to it. But so far, the way it looks, it's going to be good for the country,” he added.
Romualdez stressed that the Philippines needed to raise the value of its critical minerals with economic cooperation with the United States.
The envoy also said that the agreement with the US over Pax Silica will be transparent, which includes a possible hearing in the Senate.

Since Pax Silica is a US-led initiative, the issue was again raised with the expected visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.
Malacañang previously confirmed that Trump will visit the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit, however, it remained mum on whether the Pax Silica initiative was to be discussed.
The Pax Silica agreement is expected to be signed by November, the same month that Trump is in the Philippines. –NB, GMA News

MANILA, Philippines – The Office of the Ombudsman has filed a graft case with the Sandiganbayan against former congressman Aurelio “Dong” Gonzales Jr., one of the closest allies of former speaker Martin Romualdez in the House of Representatives.
Ombudsman Boying Remulla alleged during a press conference on Friday, October 16, that Gonzales violated the conflict-of-interest provision of the Anti-Graft Corrupt Practices Act.
“Usual story. There’s divestment, but (the money) still goes back to him. There’s no real divestment,” Remulla said.
“Payment made to the construction companies where he supposedly divested still goes to his private bank accounts,” he added.
Remulla clarified that the case filed was not plunder. In the Philippines, graft is a bailable offense.

The filing of the case came more than a year after Rappler first reported about Gonzales’ ties to A.D. Gonzales Jr. Construction, which bagged nearly P1 billion through four public works contracts from 2023 to 2024, when he was senior deputy speaker of the Romualdez-led House of Representatives.

blocks.caption: Ombudsman files flood control graft case vs Dong Gonzales

blocks.text: The former congressman is listed as an incorporator of A.D. Gonzales Construction, which registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in 1993.

It is not immediately clear when he divested from the company, but the firm’s General Information Sheet (GIS) submitted to the SEC for the last quarter of 2024 lists his children as co-owners and key officers of the firm.
Upon publication of Rappler’s original story, Gonzales denied wrongdoing.
“These are old news and old allegations that were found to be baseless by the Office of the Ombudsman more than two years ago,” Gonzales said in August 2025. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Elizabeth Struhs’ child protection case not ‘prioritised’ due to high workload, inquest hears
articles.summary:
Eight-year-old Queensland girl died in 2022 after being denied insulin by her religious parents

Elizabeth Struhs’ child protection case was not “prioritised” or worked intensively because…

blocks.text: Elizabeth Struhs’ child protection case was not “prioritised” or worked intensively because the staff member assigned to her case was “very busy”, a coroner has heard.

The Queensland coroners court also heard the case worker may have been “overly influenced” by the presentation of Struhs’ “upper class home”, putting cases that believed to involve a more immediate risk ahead of Elizabeth’s.

The eight-year-old died on 7 January 2022 of diabetic ketoacidosis, after her father, Jason Struhs, stopped providing insulin to treat her type 1 diabetes at their home in Toowoomba, Queensland. A long-term sceptic of his wife’s beliefs, he had converted to them and joined her religious sect – which subscribed to an extreme form of Christianity and denied the use of medicine – in 2021.

Coroner Ainslie Kirkegaard is holding an inquest into Elizabeth’s death. She has previously heard the eight-year-old came to the attention of child safety after a 2019 incident where she presented to hospital in a coma.
Child safety ended its involvement with the family after just 17 weeks of what was supposed to be an intensive intervention, assessing her as “safe”.

But the single child safety officer assigned to Elizabeth’s case told the court on Friday her approach wasn’t intensive and she didn’t make weekly check-ins during that period, despite departmental guidelines.

The department chose to release her back into Jason’s sole care over the objections of specialist doctors who treated Elizabeth in Brisbane, subject to a voluntary intervention with parental agreement (IPA).
The coroner heard just a single child safety officer was assigned to the case, and would often conduct home visits alone.
The officer gave evidence on Friday.

“Ideally I wanted to visit with the family at least once a week, in accordance with our IPAT (intervention with parental agreement team) guidelines,” according to her statement, presented to the court.

“During my management of the IPA for the Struhs family, I recall that I was not always available to conduct home visits with the family. I recall this being a very busy time for the CSSC (child safety service centre) and I also recall being regularly out of the office travelling to visit other families.
“I note that one of the home visits to the Struhs family was conducted by a student who was working in the team at the time.”
She said Elizabeth’s case wasn’t treated as a complex case, which it should have been due to the intervention.

But at the time, she had a “big caseload” – approximately 25-28 children in 15 families on the same intervention– she said. The coroner has previously heard that the Toowoomba region was among the busiest in the state for child safety.

Counsel assisting Simon Hamlyn-Harris said most of them were experiencing significant domestic violence, drug use, sexual abuse and it was not often that she was required to work with “upper class families” like the Struhs.
The case worker agreed that she may and may have been “overly influenced” by the presentation of the Struhs home.
“I believe that we may have prioritised other cases at the time for children who were presenting at more immediate risk,” she told the court.
She also told the court that she may have had a bias because her own child had nearly died of type 1 diabetes at age 6. She had asked not to be assigned to the case, she said.

Several witnesses have previously told the coroner they expected the intervention to last months or a year, but the case worker said they were supposed to not last longer than three months, because they were an intensive approach.
On Friday, Kirkegaard asked another child safety witness whether they felt “organisational pressure to get a matter like this finalised quickly”.
“Absolutely,” the witness said, adding an IPA could be intrusive and potentially harmful to a child if dragged out.
“I don’t believe it impacted our decision making,” she said.
On 13 November 2019, a more senior child safety officer assessed Elizabeth as “safe” and the intervention was ended.
The case worker told the coroner on Friday that she hadn’t appreciated the danger of Elizabeth’s mother’s church group, which was considered a source of support for the family.
All 14 adult members of the sect – known as the Saints – were convicted of Elizabeth’s manslaughter last year, including Elizabeth’s parents, Kerrie and Jason, and the group leader, Brendan Stevens.
In her statement she said Jason had agreed to continue to treat his daughter against his wife’s beliefs and that she had “faith” that should Kerrie stand in the way he’d leave her.
None of the witnesses can be identified for legal reasons.
The inquest continues.

articles.title: Marcos likely to meet Trump during ASEAN Summit in Manila
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and US President Donald Trump will likely meet during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in November, according to Philippine…
articles.byline: JP SORIANO, JEAN MANGALUZ, GMA News

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 3:14pm

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and US President Donald Trump will likely meet during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in November, according to Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel “Babe” Romualdez.
In an interview with GMA News, Romualdez said that they are studying Trump's possible schedule and agenda, which included a bilateral meeting between the two leaders.

“I assume that once we've confirmed the date, the exact dates of his arrival, then we can start working the schedule around that time and the agenda and the potential meetings that he will have, which includes a bilateral meeting with President Marcos,” Romualdez said.
Romualdez said that the White House directly sent confirmation of Trump’s Manila visit directly to Malacañang after Marcos invited the US President to visit the Philippines.
“Most likely, the confirmation was sent directly to the Palace,” he said.
“So I assume that this thing is confirmed. But a formal announcement, I'm sure, will be forthcoming,” he added.
Some of the topics that Trump and Marcos may discuss in the bilateral meeting include the West Philippine Sea and the Pax Silica framework agreement with the US.

The Palace previously confirmed that Trump will visit the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit. The Philippines is currently hosting the ASEAN Summit as its 2026 chair, with Singapore set to take over chairship in 2027.
In 2025, Marcos invited Trump to the Philippines while the former was in the US. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: One Nation proposes $2,000 baby subsidy in Victoria but says it won’t touch state abortion laws
articles.summary:
Announcement comes a day after Liberal and Labor parties say they will cover out-of-pocket costs for abortion care

  • Get our

blocks.text: One Nation has proposed a $2,000 baby bonus for new parents in Victoria – a day after the Labor and Liberal parties both agreed to cover out-of-pocket costs for abortion care.

The deputy leader of One Nation in Victoria, Colleen Harkin, announced the plan on Friday to remove out-of-pocket costs for pregnant women in the public healthcare system and a $2,000 subsidy for those accessing private maternity care.
She said it would cost $136m over four years but admitted it was a “ballpark” figure that would depend on how many babies were born each year.
“We don’t go hard on figures, because we actually don’t have access to the detail of this stuff,” Harkin told reporters.
She said One Nation “will not touch the abortion laws” in Victoria despite the federal party’s national platform pledging to “seek every opportunity to roll back brutal and extreme abortion law”.
“We have no state abortion policy because it is not our focus whatsoever,” Harkin said, accusing the Labor party of “lying” and “engaging with really cheap American-style scaremongering”.

On Thursday, Labor announced that, if re-elected in November, it would eliminate out-of-pocket costs for abortion care, costing $30m over four years, and claimed One Nation could use abortion as a negotiating chip with the Coalition in the event of a hung parliament.

Under Labor’s plan, private providers would be paid to deliver medical and surgical abortions up to 16 weeks’ gestation. Women would no longer have to pay for GP and specialist consultations, scans, tests or medication, which can cost up to $1,000. Those in regional Victoria who must travel long distances for care would also be eligible for a subsidy.
The government would extend access to medical abortion from nine to 10 weeks’ gestation, while commissioning a clinical review into whether it could safely be offered at up to 12 weeks’ gestation.

Within hours the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, said the Coalition would match the plan to cover out-of-pocket costs and the travel subsidy. In a statement she said “the Liberals and Nationals will not allow Labor to play politics on this issue”.
On Friday, Fiona Carroll, the wife of the premier, Ben Carroll, defended her husband for raising abortion in the leadup to the election.
“It does build on the Labor legacy, and I don’t think I’m politicising this because it is fundamental to the women in this state,” she said.
Fiona said it was “even better” the Coalition had matched the commitment, as it would “take some of that fear” out of the election for women.
Neither the Liberal party nor Labor responded to a request for comment on One Nation’s policy.

Anti-abortion activist Joanna Howe criticised Wilson, describing the Liberals as being in “lock step with Labor on every vile and evil policy” and directing her followers in Victoria to back One Nation. The Australian Christian Lobby’s Victorian director, Jasmine Yeun, said it was “getting more difficult to vote for a major party”.

But the chief executive of Women’s Health Victoria, Sally Hasler, welcomed the bipartisanship on the issue. It means no matter who is elected, Victoria will become the first state to provide abortion free.
“We are very reassured to know that it won’t be an election issue because we have support from both the ALP and the Coalition to not just protect rights but to expand rights,” Hasler said.
She described One Nation’s announcement as a deliberate attempt to frame reproductive healthcare as a choice between abortion and maternity care.
“Responding to an abortion care announcement with a maternity care announcement is a false trade-off, and it’s a deliberate one,” she said.
“It is a well-played move from the international anti-rights agenda to wind back women’s rights – one which narrowly defines women’s reproductive health.”

articles.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
articles.summary:
Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia

Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla…
articles.byline: Stefano Valentino in Sulawesi and Ajit Niranjan

blocks.text: Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction.

Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.

Ore from the Cahaya and Hengjaya mines was traced through regional smelters and Chinese processing plants run by Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, a cathode manufacturer that supplies CATL, the world’s largest battery maker. Huayou’s corporate reports list US and European carmakers as end-users, while additional corporate files and trade data show a separate route from Huayou to LG, a South Korean group that also supplies battery products to leading carmakers, via Poland.
Satellite analysis shows the mines have led to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by the indigenous Tolaki people.

“We used to ask the forest for protection in return for our offerings,” said Wadimula, a Tolaki elder whose home sits on the edge of the 21,000-hectare Cahaya mining concession. “Destroying it means destroying our own life.”

blocks.caption: Wadimula: ‘Destroying [the forest] means destroying our own life.’ Photograph: Stefano Valentino

blocks.text: Electric vehicles are less environmentally harmful than fossil fuel-burning engines, which spew gases that foul the air and heat the planet, but western carmakers have struggled to clean up supply chains for batteries built with critical minerals from Africa, Asia and South America. Environmental groups warn that a failure to curb the boom of material-hungry SUVs is exacerbating the destruction by increasing the quantity mined.

Ore from the two mining concessions is sent to a nickel smelter in an industrial complex in Morowali, on Indonesia’s eastern coast, operated by Huayou’s local subsidiary, where limonite is refined into mixed hydroxide precipitate, the primary raw material used to make battery cathodes.

In 2024, $606m worth of mixed hydroxide precipitate was shipped from the Morowali plant to ports in China, followed by further shipments worth $470m in 2025. The processed ore was transported overland to Huayou cathode manufacturing sites in Quzhou, near Shanghai, and Yulin, near the border with Vietnam.

blocks.caption: Morowali industrial park on Indonesia’s eastern coast, operated by Huayou’s local subsidiary. Photograph: Stefano Valentino

blocks.text: Public filings do not disclose specific volumes or timings of sales from Huayou to CATL, which would be needed to directly connect specific ore shipments to car batteries, but Huayou confirmed group-level supplies to CATL in response to a regulatory inquiry by the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2024. Chengdu B&M, a downstream subsidiary of Huayou, has also confirmed the supply of “large quantities” to CATL.

The investigation, published in partnership with Voxeurop and other European media partners, traced shipments from mines and refineries in Sulawesi to China, and then again from Huayou cathode and CATL battery factories to the assembly lines of carmakers in the US and Europe. Volkswagen’s facility in Braunschweig, for instance, received a shipment in October 2024 of 24 tonnes of cell modules worth about $390,000, according to data from Volza, a trade platform.

The shift to a carbon-free economy is pushing up demand for critical minerals in countries with weak environmental safeguards, though experts have argued the mining boom can be tempered without slowing the shift away from dirty fuels. In 2023, a report found lithium demand in the US transport sector could be reduced by 18% to 66% compared with a business-as-usual scenario, by improving public transport, walking and cycling more, and buying smaller cars. Better recycling could bring demand reductions as high as 92%, the report found.

Global demand for nickel is set to double to 5.5m tonnes by 2040, according to the International Energy Agency, much of it mined in Indonesia and then refined in China. The loss of trees in mining concessions means the carbon footprint of nickel from the worst mines may be up to 500 times greater than previously reported, a study in Nature Communications found last year.

The Cahaya and Hengjaya mines are located in woodlands designated as “production forest”, which are intended for forestry rather than industrial activities. However, successive Indonesian governments have weakened safeguards and carved out exemptions for miners as demand for nickel has soared.

Nickel mining may be responsible for two-thirds of the forest loss recorded since 2001 within the area encompassed by the Cahaya concession, and over half of the loss in the Hengjaya concession, spatial analysis conducted by geospatial firm TreeMap suggests.

blocks.caption: A track cut through forest in the Hengjaya concession. Photograph: Stefano Valentino

blocks.text: Sulawesi Cahaya Mineral (SCM), the company that operates the Cahaya mine, contributed to clearing an additional 330 hectares of forest in 2024, according to an analysis by Auriga, an Indonesian nonprofit. The same year, it delivered 11m tonnes of limonite ore – almost all of its production – to Huayou’s smelter. Deliveries increased to nearly 12.5m tonnes throughout 2025. The plant also continued to receive ore from the Hengjaya mine by road, local lorry drivers said.

SCM received two administrative sanctions last year for illegally clearing more than 450 hectares of forest beyond the boundaries of its permitted clearing area. The company is a subsidiary of Merdeka Battery Materials, part of a group whose shareholders include Huayou and CATL.

The carmakers identified as end-users of Huayou cathodes or recipients of shipments from CATL include Volkswagen, Volvo, Ford, General Motors, Tesla, BMW, Stellantis and Hyundai. Mercedes-Benz was separately linked to Huayou.

Many of the companies said they did not source nickel directly, they assessed and mitigated adverse impacts, and they required suppliers to comply with responsible sourcing standards. They declined to share the results of on-site audits.
Volkswagen, Europe’s leading manufacturer, which powered one-quarter of its vehicles with CATL systems in 2024, said it could not rule out that the companies may fall within its supply chain.

Volkswagen said: “We take potential risks in our supply chain very seriously. However, due to contractual obligations with our business partners, we cannot disclose specific details on our supplier relationships or their supply chain.”
Ford said: “We are committed to protecting human rights and the environment. We are reviewing the allegations and will determine any appropriate next steps based on that review.”

Mercedes-Benz said: “We take reports of environmental and social harm in raw material supply chains – including nickel from Indonesia – seriously and assess them as part of our risk-based due diligence.”

Renault Group said: “We have identified a nickel mining site in Sulawesi, Indonesia, as being a tier-n supplier (eg. indirect) in our battery supply chain. We have engaged with the relevant business partners to verify some ESG information concerning Sulawesi Cahaya Mineral.”

Volvo Cars said: “During 2025, we conducted […] onsite audits […] on suppliers [who are] part of our battery supply chains, two of them located in Indonesia […] with further battery supply chain partners during 2026 and onward.”
General Motors said: “We are aware that nickel mining in Indonesia presents significant environmental, human-rights and community-related risks.”

Stellantis said: “We are aware of the environmental and social challenges associated with nickel production in Indonesia, including risks related to deforestation, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation.”

Hyundai said: “We recognise the importance of protecting forests, biodiversity and local communities. We regularly monitor and assess our suppliers, including mineral suppliers, to ensure compliance.”
CATL, Huayou, SCM and Tesla did not respond to requests for comment. Tsingshan, the main shareholder of Nickel Industries, which operates Hengjaya mine, did not respond to a request for comment.
This investigation was supported by Journalismfund Europe and The Pulitzer Center. Lorenzo Di Stasi and James Jackson contributed reporting.

articles.title: UK could quickly re-enter EU with ‘Switzerland plus’ deal, senior MEP says
articles.summary:
Bernd Lange, who was involved in Brexit talks, says deal could be negotiated within months of any decision to deepen ties

The UK could re-enter the EU in a “Switzerland plus” package that…

blocks.text: The UK could re-enter the EU in a “Switzerland plus” package that could be negotiated within months of any decision to deepen ties with the bloc, the head of a European parliament committee has said.

Bernd Lange, who was heavily involved in Brexit negotiations, said: “I would love to see the UK back.” He said the EU missed the UK in decision-making because of its strong history of promoting open markets and democracy.

The former prime minister Boris Johnson rejected a Swiss-style relationship with the EU because it involved free movement and regulatory alignment, but it is often considered a halfway house to full membership of the bloc.

blocks.caption: A Swiss-style relationship with the EU, which is often considered a halfway house to full membership of the bloc, was rejected by the former prime minister Boris Johnson. Photograph: Neil Hall/EPA

blocks.text: Switzerland is not a member of the EU but it struck a deal last year cementing its “frictionless access” to the single market across more than 100 agreements with a new framework deal.
This gives it access to the EU’s electricity market, space programmes, Erasmus and the Digital Europe research programme, and participation in the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.
In exchange, Switzerland agreed to the free movement of people and to pay €375m (£326m) a year into the EU’s economic and cohesion funds.

Lange, a German MEP who has an important role in the European legislative process as chair of the European parliament’s trade committee, said the Switzerland framework could be a model for the UK, but it was a “passive” agreement that would not involve the country in EU decision-making.

“As a step by step [process], of course, there are a lot of possibilities, but I would love to have the UK come back also in the political decision-making process and politically be engaged. So we have the model of Switzerland … Switzerland plus, I would say, as that has some kinds of engagement but not the full membership.”

He said the decision about what relationship the UK wanted with the EU was entirely “in the hands of the UK”, but if it opted for something like Switzerland plus, an agreement could be achieved quickly, notwithstanding political hiccups.
He was speaking in London, where his schedule includes a meeting with the trade minister, Anas Sarwar, who is part of a team working on the UK’s new position on EU relations.

blocks.caption: Bernd Lange, the chair of the European parliament’s trade committee, said he supported Andy Burnham’s call for the UK not to be locked out of the EU’s Made in Europe legislation. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP

blocks.text: Lange also threw his weight behind Andy Burnham’s call for the EU not to lock the UK out of Made in Europe legislation that would restrict UK suppliers from inclusion in public procurement tenders as well as some corporate contracts such as car fleets.

French and German leaders were reportedly close on Thursday to agreeing a proposal that the UK could be included, provided it aligned with the EU’s 2024 tariffs on imports of Chinese electric vehicles.
This week the boss of Mercedes said the EU would be making a “deliberate choice” to harm the EU car industry if it did not allow the UK into the Made in Europe package.
after newsletter promotion

Burnham has backing from the Netherlands, Germany and Italy. France, which came up with the legislative proposals, was opposed, saying it needed to get the legislation on the books urgently to guard against cheap competition from China, and that allowing the UK and other allied countries in could hold up the lawmaking.
Lange said the UK should “of course” be included because it was already aligned with the EU on environmental standards and employment laws.

blocks.caption: A Mercedes-Benz factory in Germany. The boss of Mercedes this week called for the UK to be included in the Made in Europe package. Photograph: Christoph Steitz/Reuters

blocks.text: He said France’s position was “not rational” and “also so emotional” but could be born from the desire to be seen as putting France first before next April’s presidential elections, in which Marine Le Pen, who is opposed to globalism, could take power.

Locking the UK out of Made in Europe could also cause a legal dispute over the trade and cooperation agreement that allows UK goods to be sold in the single market without barriers as long as they the meet the bloc’s standards.

The Made in Europe package, or the Industrial Accelerator Act, is expected to get political approval by the end of the year or early 2027, meaning Burnham does not have much time to get clauses inserted designating the UK as European for the purposes of the legislation.
But Lange said there could be time after that, given the processes of the European parliament, where three committees have scrutinising powers.
“There are 5,100 amendments,” he said, referring to the protracted process ahead, including one on UK inclusion.

articles.title: UK law could deny Fayed accusers recognition as victims of human trafficking
articles.summary:
‘Unfair’ immigration and asylum bill could fail to support sexual violence survivors, anti-slavery commissioner says

Survivors of sexual violence could wrongly be denied recognition as…

blocks.text: Survivors of sexual violence could wrongly be denied recognition as victims of human trafficking under credibility tests in a new UK law, the independent anti-slavery commissioner has warned.

Eleanor Lyons said the measures in the immigration and asylum bill were fundamentally unfair and could lead to many more victims of slavery and trafficking, including those allegedly abused by Mohamed Al Fayed, being denied support.
Under the legislation, Home Office officials must regard any delay to making a claim of modern day slavery or human trafficking as damaging to their credibility.
Any inaccuracy, inconsistency or omission in a person’s account, as well as any striking similarity to a claim made by someone else, must also be viewed as reasons for disbelief.

Lyons said the credibility tests would harm survivors of sexual violence who often suffered memory loss as a result of their trauma. Many were also reluctant to come forward to disclose their exploitation due to fear of reprisals by their abusers, she added.

“They are basically saying to victims, if you don’t come forward in a timely fashion not yet defined, if there are inconsistencies in your account, and if there are similarities between exploitation and [those of] others, the Home Office decision-maker must question your credibility,” Lyons said.

“For the Al Fayed victims [that] would be particularly concerning because a lot of time has passed [since the alleged abuse], a lot of them were sadly exploited in similar ways to each other, and some of the things that happened to them were completely horrific and they may not be able to recall exactly what time, which place they happened in [due to the impact of trauma].”

Several women who were allegedly sexually abused by Fayed, said they feared the measures would undermine investigations into what they described as the late billionaire’s international trafficking network.

blocks.caption: Holly Johnson, pictured aged 24 when she worked at Harrods, said the credibility tests will re-victimise survivors.

blocks.text: Holly Johnson, who says she was trafficked and sexually abused when she worked at Harrods and Fayed’s Park Lane offices, said the credibility tests would re-victimise survivors.

She added: “Fayed had a specific strategy for trafficking and assaulting women, and many of our stories are really similar. To say someone shouldn’t be believed because their situation is too similar to another victim of that same abuser is absurd.”

No One Above, a collective of survivors of Fayed’s alleged abuse, said many women delayed reporting their exploitation until after his death in 2023 and Harrods’ declaration in 2024 that those who signed non-disclosure agreements would not have them enforced.

Elizabeth, an NOA member who has been recognised as a trafficking victim by the Home Office, said: “It took that for me to finally believe that I couldn’t have somebody take my house away for speaking out.”

Pelham Spong, who says she was trafficked in Paris on Fayed’s orders in 2008 before being sent to London to be sexually assaulted by him, said she did not go to the Met police until 2017 because she feared her life “was going to be ruined”.

blocks.caption: Pelham Spong, who says she was sent to London to be sexually assaulted by Fayed, said the thought of speaking out against him as a 23-year-old was ‘unfathomable’. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian

blocks.text: “The thought of speaking out as a 23-year-old with no money, no resources behind me against a billionaire was unfathomable,” said Spong, whose case is being investigated by the French police. “He was so powerful.”

The government has introduced the credibility tests to close what it characterises as opportunities to misuse the National Referral Mechanism (NRM), the system for identifying potential victims of modern slavery and human trafficking in the UK, and to speed up the removal and deportation of illegal migrants.

Eleanora Fais, the anti-trafficking monitoring group coordinator at Anti-Slavery International, said: “If your primary aim is to introduce legislation that is focused on immigration enforcement, safeguarding will come in second place.

“The NRM was always meant to help survivors to disclose and be referred to support needed for the recovery. Alongside that, if they wished to, they could cooperate with police to ensure that perpetrators were brought to justice. If you introduce these criteria to weaken the system, that’s not going to happen.”

Hilary Agg, the head of policy and research at the anti-slavery charity Unseen, said the measures would allow human trafficking to thrive in the UK because fewer victims would be identified and be able to help police to pursue perpetrators.
She added that the tests would harm immigrants and the majority of trafficking and slavery victims, who are British nationals.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Modern slavery is a barbaric crime, and the government is committed to identifying victims and ensuring they get the support they need. The immigration and asylum bill will strengthen protections and crack down on exploitation, while reducing opportunities for improper use of the system.
“The credibility considerations in the bill are well-balanced and contain appropriate safeguards, which will enhance the robustness of modern slavery decision-making.”
A Harrods spokesperson said it supported all survivors in their pursuit of justice and continued to work closely with the Met police on its investigation.

A Ritz Paris spokesperson said it was “deeply concerned by the allegations that have been reported and takes them with the utmost seriousness. We would like to express our deepest sympathy to the women who have come forward.”
The Fayed estate has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Exclusive Brethren head denies knowing church members were volunteering for Liberal party during 2025 election
articles.summary:
Bruce Hales also denies church was a cult while son tells parliamentary committee it was ‘a bit rough’ being labelled as such

  • Get our

blocks.text: The most senior member of the Exclusive Brethren has denied any knowledge of or involvement in thousands of members from his church volunteering for the Liberal party at the 2025 election.

The Plymouth Brethren christian church has rejected claims it coordinated volunteers and a campaign for the Coalition, and that it secretly paid far-right figures to stage stunts against the prime minister and other Labor MPs.

The fiery parliamentary committee hearing on Friday was marred by clashes, with members of the committee accusing one another of “religious persecution” and “running a protection racket” for the church.
Bruce Hales, the Brethren’s most senior member, said he had no involvement or knowledge of church members volunteering for the Coalition.
“I want to be clear and unequivocal. I had no involvement whatsoever in relation to any members who volunteered or took part in any aspect of the 2025 federal election,” he told the inquiry.
“I did not plan such activities. I did not coordinate such activities. I did not direct such activities. I did not fund such activities.”
Hales denied that his church was a cult, a term used by the prime minister, while his son, Gareth Hales, who also appeared before the committee, said it was “a bit rough” being labelled as such.

Gareth Hales gave evidence on Friday he had met Morgan C Jonas and Chris de Bruyne separately in a business capacity, and briefly discussed the “general direction the government was headed”. The independent MP Andrew Gee referred to the two as far-right activists, although Gareth Hales denied knowing their political affiliations at the time.

Nine newspapers have reported Jonas and de Bruyne were involved in a campaign that targeted Labor and other left-leaning politicians during the election. Gareth Hales denied reports his company Sante Global paid the two men to disrupt other campaigns.
There was turmoil in the committee as Coalition members likened questioning by Labor and crossbench MPs to a “Spanish Inquisition”.

Nationals senator Bridget McKenzie and Liberal MP Ben Small repeatedly interrupted questions, calling them “disgraceful” and “disrespectful”. McKenzie said the line of questioning looked “a lot like religious persecution”, while Small was accused of trying to answer questions for the church.
Gee, who was previously a Nationals MP, said the two were running an “old Liberal party protection racket”, a comment he was forced to withdraw.

On 20 April 2025, just under two weeks before the federal election, Bruce Hales gave a sermon where he told members to be “fervent in prayer for good government”, and that the country needed to be happy again and smiling again.
after newsletter promotion

The latter two phrases were seen on posters endorsing the Liberal party during the campaign. Bruce Hales denied his sermon was a call to action and said he had no knowledge of his words being used in billboards and advertising at the election.

Nine newspapers reported the sermon had been broadcast and then turned into a text message by Gareth Hale and his brothers, which said, “We need to make sure our booths are manned and our volunteers are fired up.”

Gareth Hales, who has no official role in the church, said he could not confirm or deny whether he had written this message but denied instructing members to join the campaign. He said he had encouraged members who had already been volunteering to “keep doing what they were doing”.
Gee, who claimed he was tailed by several Brethren members in his regional New South Wales electorate, said it “defies belief” that the church had no role in coordinating volunteers.
Gareth Hales said they were not acting as members of the church.

“I can understand it’s difficult to believe but they weren’t members of the church, they were members of concerned business groups and members of private citizens – they weren’t there on behalf of the church,” Gareth Hales said.
Gee replied: “I, for one, am not buying what you are selling but I do appreciate you giving evidence today.”

articles.title: Pornography showing strangulation and incest to be banned in UK from early November
articles.summary:
Campaigners welcome new legislation which follows 2025 review into pornography regulation

Pornography that depicts strangulation and incestuous relationships will be banned from early…

blocks.text: Pornography that depicts strangulation and incestuous relationships will be banned from early November, the UK government has announced.
The content will be outlawed from 6 November after cross-party pressure prompted ministers to announce new legislation earlier this year.
Online pornography depicting strangulation or suffocation, sex between people who are related or pretending to be related, or when somebody is pretending to be a child under 16, will be illegal.

The justice minister, Alex Davies-Jones, said: “This isn’t about criminalising harmless sexual preferences. But porn can shape what people think a healthy relationship looks like, especially young people.
“Content that normalises, or even glorifies, violence against women is dangerous and can blur the line with what is acceptable in real life.”
The Conservative peer Gabby Bertin made the recommendations in her review into pornography regulation which reported in 2025.
Her report found pornography that shows women being choked can have “devastating” real-world consequences.
It highlighted “disturbing” role-play, including incest and adults portraying children. Both will be banned.
The report said there had been a “total absence of government scrutiny” of the pornography industry.
Non-fatal strangulation is already an offence in its own right, but it is not illegal to show it online.
Reacting to the announcement, Lady Bertin said: “It is very good news these offences will come into force, and not a moment too soon.

“This change in law alongside better enforcement and stronger regulation will send the unequivocal signal not only to the companies that host and facilitate porn but also to wider society that extreme and violent content that encourages real-life harm is not acceptable.”
The End Violence Against Women Coalition campaign group welcomed the ban, urging ministers to ensure it is enforced.

Its interim director, Janaya Walker, said: “This is an important step towards tackling the normalisation of violence against women and girls, and the result of years of campaigning by EVAW and other experts who have raised concerns about the impact of violent pornography.
“Strangulation can cause serious, lasting harm and even death, yet its widespread portrayal in pornography risks normalising this violence in sexual relationships, particularly among young people.

“The introduction of this offence is an important recognition of the harm caused by violent pornography and the need to hold an industry accountable for content that depicts and profits from violence against women and girls.
“The government must now ensure the ban is effectively enforced, and update the Online Safety Act so that online platforms are required to remove this content.”

articles.title: DILG tags ex-Bangsamoro MP in P3.5B shabu smuggling try from Laos
articles.summary: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Friday identified the Mindanao politician allegedly involved in the attempted smuggling of P3.5 billion worth of shabu from Laos to the Philippines as former…

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 2:44pm

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Friday identified the Mindanao politician allegedly involved in the attempted smuggling of P3.5 billion worth of shabu from Laos to the Philippines as former Bangsamoro Parliament member Edriezan Hadji Nasser Rimbang.

Remulla said this at a Palace briefing as he presented a link diagram of the individuals allegedly involved in the planned smuggling of 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu.
“Sultan Edriezan Rimbang is believed to be the financier of the entire operation,” Remulla said.
“Edrieza Rimbang Nasser was a former member of parliament. Natalo siya nung huling (he lost in the recent) election,” he added.
GMA News Online is trying to get a comment from Rimbang and will publish his comment as soon as it is available.

Remulla said that Rimbang is in the same political party as former president Rodrigo Duterte, but clarified that authorities are not labeling any ethnicity, city, or people and are simply putting names to the faces of the persons of interest.

“But this is to counter the narrative that people are developing that people from Manila are the ones involved in this caper. This operation was between Sultan Edriezan Rimbang Nasser and his cohorts,” Remulla said.

On Thursday, the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) said a politician from Mindanao allegedly provided the funds for the private plane that would have been used to smuggle the illegal drugs. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Romualdez camp confronts 'maleta boy' witness over affidavit 'errors,' recantations
articles.summary: The camp of former speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez confronted prosecution witness Rodante Orbillo over his signature in a February 2026 joint affidavit of 18 former bodyguards of…

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 2:44pm

The camp of former speaker and Leyte Representative Martin Romualdez confronted prosecution witness Rodante Orbillo over his signature in a February 2026 joint affidavit of 18 former bodyguards of former Ako Bicol party-list representative Zaldy Co, which contained errors as stated by Orbillo's counsel, Levito Baligod.

Lawyer Rashel Ann Pomoy, counsel for Romualdez, made the move during Day 3 of Romualdez's bail petition hearing. She played videos in court of Baligod saying that the February 2026 joint affidavit of 18 ex-bodyguards made an error in including Senator Loren Legarda and ML party-list Representative Leila de Lima.

Pomoy said the February 2026 affidavit was the root of the subsequent allegations made against Romualdez and other public officials, and was announced in a press conference where Orbillo was present, ultimately resulting in the filing of P7.4-billion plunder charge against her client in September this year.
Asked by Pomoy if he was aware of Baligod's statements that the February affidavit contained errors, Orbillo answered in the affirmative.
The prosecution panel objected to the defense's line of questioning, saying that Orbillo cannot answer for Baligod's pronouncements.
Pomoy, however, argued that Orbillo can be confronted with such questions since he signed the February 2026 affidavit.

"He is one of the affiants (signatories) of the affidavit as indicated by Atty. Baligod. These [errors] directly affect the matters of the affidavit because [there are] affiants who have recanted inclusion of certain individuals, and that Atty. Baligod said these were errors," Pomoy said.
"We want to know who is the person that is behind them coming out and saying these things," Pomoy added.

During her cross examination on Orbillo, Pomoy also invoked the recantation made by Mark Bunagan and Dennis Loma, given that Orbillo stated in his August 2026 affidavit submitted to the Ombudsman that he was with the two individuals in his money deliveries to Romualdez.
Orbillo said he was not aware of the recantation of Bunagan and Loma.
"Hindi ko alam iyong pinapasinungalingan," Orbillo said.
(I do not know what they are disputing.)

Romualdez's counsel also asked Orbillo if he was aware that alleged whistleblower Orly Guteza, Rosebert Waupan and Benny Boluntante, who are among the 18 ex-bodyguards of Co, already recanted their statements against Romualdez.
Orbillo answered in the affirmative.
During the redirect examination of the prosecution, Orbillo also said he delivered money in suitcases to Romualdez at least 10 times, but that Romualdez was not present in those deliveries.

Asked by Sandiganbayan Third Division chairperson and Associate Justice Karl Miranda what made him testify even if there were offers of money worth P15 million to P20 million as claimed by Orbillo, he answered: "Kung kumagat po kami sa offer nilang iyon, wala na pong magsasalita sa nangyaring korapsyon sa flood control."
Miranda responded by reminding Orbillo that he should only speak for himself.
"Don't speak for the others. Ang tinatanong ko, ikaw (I'm asking you)," the magistrate said.
Orbillo said he testified "para sa bayan (for the nation)."
Miranda responded that it is always easier to speak big.
"Madaling magsabi na para sa bayan, lalo na kung malalaking amount ang involved (It's easy to say that it's for the nation, especially if huge amounts are involved)," he said.
Orbillo replied by saying, "Gusto lang po namin maglahad ng katotohanan (I only want to reveal the truth)." — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sandro Marcos confirms transfer to Lakas-CMD
articles.summary: House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos of Ilocos Norte on Friday confirmed that he has joined Lakas-CMD.

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 2:40pm
House Majority Leader Sandro Marcos of Ilocos Norte has confirmed that he has joined Lakas-CMD.
In an interview with local media, Marcos said he jumped ship from his father’s political party, Partido Federal ng Pilipinas, to Lakas-CMD to fill in Lakas-CMD’s leadership void.

Congressman Marcos’ uncle, former Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez, is the Lakas-CMD president but is in detention due to a pending P7.4 billion plunder scam due to his alleged involvement in the flood control scam.

“It was simple. I met with the Speaker [Bojie Dy of Isabela] and he noticed na ang Lakas ngayon, walang ulo. No one is leading Lakas. The Speaker told me that PFP members are already well taken care of in the sense that the President, the Speaker, Senior Deputy Speaker and almost all House leaders are with PFP,” Marcos said in an interview with local media in Ilocos Norte.
Lakas-CMD is the biggest political party in the House of Representatives with at least 70 members.

“The Speaker told me that it would be better for me to transfer to Lakas so the Lakas members in the House will have someone to talk to over their concerns, because the PFP already have the Speaker in their ranks. They (Lakas members) [as it is] did not have anyone to go to within the party that had a leadership position influential enough to be able to help with their districts and constituencies,” Marcos added.
Congressman Marcos is the son of President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr.
“This is an administrative matter so that the members of Lakas don’t feel lost,” Marcos said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Matibag says he is 'nobody' if mansions, firms are basis
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Friday said Vice President Sara Duterte"s remark that he is a “nobody” is "true" if the basis is having mansions and receiving profit…

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 2:27pm

National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Friday said Vice President Sara Duterte’s remark that he is a “nobody” is "true" if the basis is having mansions and receiving profit from Chinese state-owned companies.

“Well, totoo naman ‘yun kung ang basehan ay mga mansion, mga negosyo, mga Jollibee ganyan, at kung may natatanggap na malaking pera sa Chinese state-owned companies, ay nobody talaga,” he said in an ambush interview

(Well, that’s true if the basis is mansions, businesses, Jollibee stores, and things like that, and if someone is receiving large amounts of money from Chinese state-owned companies, then they really are nobody.)
Earlier, Duterte called Matibag a nobody when asked for a comment on the NBI chief's challenge to file a case if she thinks he is biased or doing something wrong.

This comes amid the NBI’s investigation into claims of dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that he delivered cash to the vice president and others on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The NBI is also probing the real properties listed in the vice president’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs).
Meanwhile, AMLC records showed that P5.3 billion in covered and suspicious transactions were flagged across 15 companies linked to Duterte and her husband.

Among these is Cale88 Foods Corporation, which reportedly received an estimated P319 million from China and Hong Kong. Senator-judges also flagged several companies recorded in the transactions as state-owned Chinese entities.
Duterte’s camp has maintained that there is no proof directly linking millions of pesos in her and her husband’s bank accounts to funds from the Chinese government.
Matibag said the NBI will continue its investigation. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: India's 'Cockroaches' to march again after protest crackdown
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party has called on people to gather at New Delhi's central business district to wave the Indian national flag as it asserts a right to protest. DW has more.

image.caption: Thousands of youth protesters, including CJP and student leaders, were detained last weekend after police denied them permission to protestImage: Priyanshu Singh/REUTERS

blocks.text: Live
The Cockroach Janta Party has called on people to gather at New Delhi's central business district to wave the Indian national flag as it asserts a right to protest. DW has more.

blocks.caption: Thousands of youth protesters, including CJP and student leaders, were detained last weekend after police denied them permission to protestImage: Priyanshu Singh/REUTERS

blocks.text: What you need to know
Here are the latest developments from India on Friday, October 16:

items: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) slated to hold 'Lehra Do Tiranga' (Wave The Tricolor) rally
Prime Minister Narendra Modi to visit Canada from December 11-12
Indian Embassy calls on nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain calm and alert amid intensifying Houthi strikes

blocks.text: Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
October 16, 2026
What do we know about CJP's planned 'Tiranga March'?
With its previous mass demonstration foiled, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is now campaigning to claim a right to protest — about 600 meters (1,970 feet) away from Jantar Mantar.
Friday's planned protest, featuring the national flag, is scheduled to be held at 5 p.m. local time (1130 UTC) at Central Park in Connaught Place, a prime commercial hub in central Delhi.
"Let's Gather In Large Numbers And Wave Our National Flag. Let's Stand In Support Of Ashutosh and Saurav!" the CJP said, referring to two of the movement's leaders currently being held in detention.
The New Delhi Municipal Corporation, meanwhile, has shut down Central Park for two days, citing "administrative reasons."
Delhi Police said in a statement that prohibitory orders, aimed at maintaining peace and ensuring public safety, were in force in and around Connaught Place.
It called on protesters to not participate in any gathering that violates the orders.

"However, the Delhi Police may consider making arrangements to permit a select group of individuals to gather at a suitable location for the purpose of carrying the national flag and singing the national anthem," Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said.
Reports on Friday morning said that security at Connaught Place remains tight. A traffic advisory has been issued for the area.
On Thursday, the Delhi High Court declined to stop the CJP's Connaught Place protest.

"Do we need to take permission to wave our Indian flag?" the 'Cockroach' movement said in a post on X. The CJP posted an emoji of the Indian flag, saying it "belongs to the 1.3 Billion people of this country and not the Delhi police. We will wave it where we want!"

Meanwhile, another "Lehra Do Tiranga" rally called by the CJP in India's financial capital of Mumbai on Friday has received a go-ahead from the city police. The protest is expected to take place at Azad Maidan.

articles.title: Trump calls Ukraine’s resumption of strikes on Russian oil refineries a ‘disgrace’
articles.summary:
US president says Zelenskyy ‘more difficult ​to deal with ​than Putin’ after so-called energy ceasefire collapses

Donald Trump has called Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries…

blocks.text: Donald Trump has called Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries a “disgrace”, while renewing his criticism of Volodymyr ⁠Zelenskyy after an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine collapsed.

Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries ⁠after Zelenskyy said that Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire abruptly declared by Trump last week, one that neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to.
“All he’s doing is making the world oil price higher. Well, I think that’s a disgrace,” the US president told the Newsmax news outlet in an interview aired on Thursday.

“There are a lot ‌of targets you can ‌hit, but when you shoot at diesel refineries where you make, you know, ‌diesel oil, and we need that, and the world needs that, then he’s not doing a good service for the world.”
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel on to global markets.

Zelenskyy slammed the agreement, which was widely interpreted as an attempt to curb high fuel prices ahead of the US midterm election, saying it would allow Russia to press on with its full-scale invasion of Ukraine that began more than four and a half years ago. US efforts under Trump to end the war have made no progress.

Trump repeated to Newsmax his views of the two leaders involved in the conflict. “I’m not a big fan of Zelenskyy,” Trump said. “I think they actually both would like to see it ⁠end, but I think I find Zelenskyy to be more difficult ​to deal with ​than Putin.”

Kyiv’s relationship with Washington was strained further this week when Ukraine said Starlink services had been restricted, in effect hobbling Ukrainian drone strike missions and crucial air defences with a flick of the switch.
During a visit to London this week, the Ukrainian president said the sudden restriction of Starlink had left him feeling personally betrayed by Trump and lamented losing a partner.

British defence secretary Wes Streeting said on Thursday his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, had assured him in a face-to-face meeting that the vital satellite communications system had been restored. In an interview with the BBC, he said it was unclear what had caused the disruption, but added: “This is not the first time we’ve seen a falling out between Washington and Kyiv.”

Amid growing doubts about long-term US commitment to Ukraine, European leaders have shown their support for Zelenskyy, who met Nato chief Mark Rutte in Brussels and held a string of bilateral meetings before he was set to join an EU summit on Friday.
After meeting Zelenskyy, French president Emmanuel Macron said it was “crucial” that Ukraine receive “all the means necessary to protect itself”.
“I can reassure you, dear Ukrainian friends and President Zelenskyy: YOU ARE NOT ALONE,” Polish prime minister Donald Tusk posted online.
As he met with Macron in Brussels, Zelensky said that the Kremlin had “launched yet another vile drone strike on Ukrainian energy infrastructure” in the city of Lutsk, which caused blackouts.
The Kremlin meanwhile accused Ukraine of derailing US peace efforts by resuming its strikes on refineries.

articles.title: NBI issues subpoenas to 'Machong Chismisan' podcast members
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has issued subpoenas to members of the "Machong Chismisan" podcast following their remarks about Joshua "Josh" Aquino, the son of Kris Aquino.

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 1:38pm
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has issued subpoenas to members of the "Machong Chismisan" podcast following their remarks about Joshua "Josh" Aquino, the son of Kris Aquino.

According to the NBI, the members were asked to appear at different times before the bureau on October 20, Tuesday, to shed light on its investigation regarding alleged violations of the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons, in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

The podcast garnered flak over a now-deleted episode titled "Ang Pagbabalik Ni Kris Aquino," in which the hosts made disparaging remarks about Josh by comparing him with his younger brother, Bimby, and making derogatory remarks about his disability.
Following the backlash, "Machong Chismisan" took down the episode and apologized to the entire Aquino family.
The Pod Network also terminated its contract with the podcast.
According to Sam Nielsen's report on Super Radyo dzBB, two members have received their subpoenas.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag also reportedly said the podcast members' apology is not enough to erase criminal liability.
TV host Boy Abunda, who has been vocal about his support for Josh, has previously said that if Kris were to ask him, he would advise her to file charges against the alleged offenders.

In a post on Instagram, Kris said she opted not to release a statement in response to "what were irresponsible & uninformed opinions" as she didn't want to give them the "word war" they were expecting. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte was told prosecutors might drop 3 impeachment charges
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte and her defense team had an inkling that House prosecutors would reduce the impeachment case against her to a single charge, as rumors of the move had already been abound,…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 1:32pm

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte and her defense team had an inkling that House prosecutors would reduce the impeachment case against her to a single charge, as rumors of the move had already been abound, two of her defense lawyers said.

In separate interviews, defense spokesperson Michael Poa and deputy spokesperson Justin Nicol Gular said Duterte was told of the possible withdrawal before prosecutors formally made a motion for it on Tuesday, October 13. At the time the vice president was briefed, she had wanted to think things over before acting.

"Actually, when I heard the rumors, I already updated her," Poa said on ANC's "Headstart" on Thursday, October 15. "When I spoke to her right after, all she said to me was, 'You know what, let's sleep on this. Let's think about things first.'"
"She wasn't surprised because, as we said, she had been informed beforehand of the possibility," Gular said in Filipino in an interview with One PH on Thursday.
The prosecution on Tuesday withdrew Article I on the alleged misuse of confidential funds, Article III on alleged bribery at the Department of Education and Article IV on alleged grave threats.
Only Article II, on unexplained wealth, remains.
The Senate impeachment court accepted the withdrawal and lifted the sub judice rule on the three dropped charges, allowing both sides to discuss them in public.
Poa said he would meet Duterte in the coming days because the defense must file a manifestation stating her position on the ruling.
Days before the hearing, the defense had been picking up "chismis" or gossip, that prosecutors might drop three articles, Gular said.
But as the defense team prepared for October 13, formally, only one withdrawal was certain, Gular said, as prosecutors had already filed a manifestation to drop the bribery charge.
"We receive a lot of information during the course of this trial. But you never know if it will happen or turn out to be true," Gular said.
Why the defense objects
Poa said the defense's first reaction to the lifting of the sub judice rule was that it creates "complications."
The grave threats charge is one article that Duterte's lawyers cannot yet speak about in public, as a regional trial court hearing Duterte's separate criminal case has issued a gag order, Poa said.
The defense spokesperson also lamented the limitations that would come with defending allegations at a press conference and not in court.
Some witnesses the defense wanted to subpoena "are not necessarily aligned with us," Poa said, and could not be summoned to a press conference.

He would not speculate on whether the court will still let the defense call witnesses on the dropped charges. The burden is on the defense to show they are relevant, he said, and prosecutors have the right to object.
"We also don't want to be seen as wasting the time of the court. But again, fairness is something we've always asked for," Poa said.
'Court still trying to balance' issues, Poa acknowledges
Asked whether the court has remained fair, Poa said, "I would like to say yes."
"I don't want to say the court is unfair because the court is still trying to balance the situation, as I've seen the presiding officer do," he said.
"Without casting aspersions on the prosecution, perhaps they had a strategy that they had to tweak along the way," Poa said.
The defense will begin presenting its evidence on November 9. The trial is on hold while the Senate takes up the proposed 2027 national budget.
Asked if the defense would likely finish before Christmas, Poa said: "I don't want to box us in to a schedule. It's not about delaying or prolonging the proceedings or shortening the proceedings."
The withdrawal forced the defense to "restrategize," he said, and it may drop witnesses or call others it had held in reserve.
"I think all of us would want to finish, personally, before Christmas, but we can't box the defense in," Poa said.

But will the vice president take the stand? Poa said: "If there's a trigger point, meaning aspects of the case that we feel may only be explained by the vice president herself or attorney Mans Carpio himself, we will have to advise them," he said.
"But at the end of the day, it will be their decision if they want to take the stand or not," he added.
Article II accuses Duterte of having unlawful business interests and amassing wealth she did not declare in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

articles.title: Senators: PH won't back down despite Chinese envoy's 'threats'
articles.summary: Several senators on Friday strongly denounced the supposed threats of Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan that Beijing could “easily win” against the Philippines if it resorted to force.

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 1:31pm
Several senators on Friday strongly denounced the supposed threats of Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan that Beijing could “easily win” against the Philippines if it resorted to force.
Senate committee on foreign relations vice chairman Erwin Tulfo stressed that the Philippines’ resolve to settle maritime issues with China must not be mistaken for weakness.

“Let there be no doubt: Nobody in this world can bully the Philippines—whether through words or by force. Our sovereignty is not negotiable, our dignity is not for sale, and our resolve must never be mistaken for weakness,” Tulfo said.

“We do not take lightly the statement that China can ‘easily win’ if it uses force against the Philippines. As a peace-loving country that upholds democracy and international law, the Filipino people will not back down in the face of these threats,” he added.
Tulfo said that Filipinos will fight for the country’s sovereignty if threatened, just like in the past.

“We fought foreign invaders in the past with only crude weapons but a lot of courage, sweat, and blood - and we succeeded. We will do so again if our sovereignty is threatened once more. Sa Pilipino ang Pilipinas. Hindi kami pasisiil,” he said.
(The Philippines belongs to the Filipinos. We will not be oppressed.)
Senator Risa Hontiveros, meanwhile, described Jing’s statements as “gray zone aggression in diplomatic form, meant to intimidate and coerce while stopping just short of war.”
She said that China must be held accountable for Jing’s words and their actions in the West Philippine Sea.

“Let it be clear to China that no threat will make us surrender what is rightfully ours. The Philippines has only done what every law-abiding member of the community of nations would do—defend our rights through legal and diplomatic means,” Hontiveros said.
“An ambassador who threatens his host country has crossed a line. Summoning him is not enough,” she said.

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday confirmed he will summon the Chinese Ambassador following his remarks, which the chief executive said “sounds very much like a threat, and it is not a very diplomatic statement to be made.”
Hontiveros said the Philippine government should instead demand a formal retraction and apology from Beijing over Jing’s statement.
“If none comes, the ambassador should be declared persona non grata,” she said.

“The Philippines must also raise this threat before ASEAN and the United Nations General Assembly. When one nation is threatened, every member-state that values international law is threatened too,” she added.

A social media post by Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela, showed Jing being interviewed, where he said, "If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force. You know, we love peace, and in this region, we enjoy the peace."
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) urged the Chinese ambassador to exercise greater restraint in his public statements after his controversial remarks. —AOL, GMA News
